name: stranded-dirty-files
question: Which dirty files in this project have no live owner and predate the most recent finalize commit?
cost_provenance: measured 2026-06-12 on the ULDF framework repo under Git Bash (win32; slowest supported environment) -- pessimistic-honest per ORACLE-COST-01; under-declaration causes timeout kills

schema.has_stranded: boolean (true iff count > 0; false when count == 0 OR count == -1)
schema.count: integer (number of stranded files; -1 means detection skipped — too many dirty files >2000)
schema.oldest_mtime: string|null (ISO-8601 UTC mtime of the oldest stranded file; null when count == 0 OR detection skipped)
schema.sample: array (capped at 10) of {path: string, mtime: ISO-8601 UTC, age_days: int}
schema.live_peer_count: integer (number of live peers consulted for ownership; 0 when registry missing)
schema.provably_unowned: integer (of the `count` reported strands, how many are proved un-owned by the STRAND-02 mtime-ordering test -- mtime older than the earliest live peer's spawnedAt. Equals `count` when live_peer_count == 0, since with no live peer the proposition is vacuously true. 0 when the proof could not run at all -- a live peer with an absent or unparseable spawnedAt disables it for the whole run. Added in 1.3.0 -- DEFER-193 / DEC-372; ADDITIVE to the frozen schema per its own change rule.)
schema.attribution: string enum: 'measured' (a live peer published a dirtyFiles array -- complete by construction, so an absent path is evidence of non-ownership. RESERVED, NOT PRODUCED: nothing in the framework writes registry dirtyFiles[] -- DISC-ORA-12 -- so this grade cannot occur anywhere today; kept because it is authoritative if a producer ever appears and because already-deployed consumers map it) | 'predates-peers' (STRAND-02: EVERY reported strand file's mtime is older than the earliest live peer's spawnedAt, so no visible live peer can have written any of them -- a peer that had would have set the mtime at or after its own start. This is the reachable top of the ladder and the grade a sweep-with-peers-present is earned by. All-or-nothing over the reported set, because the sweep it gates is all-or-nothing) | 'journal-partial' (attribution came only from live peers' write journals, which record TOOL CALLS and cannot see script or external writes, so a journal MISS is not evidence -- hits still filter, but the sweep recommendation is withheld) | 'unavailable' (live peers exist and supplied neither) | 'no-peers' (no live peer in this project) | 'not-measured' (detection skipped). Added in 1.2.0 -- DEFER-039/DEFER-190; 'predates-peers' added in 1.3.0 -- DEFER-193/DEC-372; both ADDITIVE to the frozen schema per its own change rule (DEC-366, DEC-372).
schema.last_finalize_at: string|null (ISO-8601 UTC commit timestamp of HEAD; null when not in a git repo OR no commits)
schema.briefing: string (empty when no stranded files; populated when count > 0 OR count == -1)

Do NOT sweep; inspect with /0-uldf-oracle stranded-dirty-files"  (attribution == 'journal-partial'; takes precedence over the small/large forms)
_briefingForms._withheld_proved_clause:
Both withholding forms carry an extra sentence when the STRAND-02 proof could run: "

of predate every live peer's session start; do not." -- so a refusal says how much of the list IS proved instead of refusing opaquely (DEC-360's escape-chain requirement applied to the report). Absent when the proof could not run at all (no live peers, or a peer with no spawnedAt).

scope_guard.rationale: Above 2000 dirty files, mtime stat + per-file ownership probe blows the briefing budget. Oracle returns count: -1 sentinel; user runs /0-uldf-finalize --include-stranded for the full audit.

consultation.notes: Cheap, and gracefully absent on clean projects. Also consumed by /0-uldf-finalize --include-stranded flag handling. This prose lived in typical_sessions_using until DEC-346; that field is compared as an exact token by briefing-oracles.{sh,ps1}, so the sentence silently cost this oracle its briefing admission and its CSI-15 line never fired in any project that installed it. DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE from the GitCellar reference (DEFER-190 port): GitCellar demoted its copy to on-demand for briefing-budget reasons; the template keeps 'every' because oracle-manifest-admission-smoke.sh B7 asserts this manifest is ADMITTED, and post-hardening the briefing line is honest in every branch (the trust reason for demotion is gone).

assertion.asserts: Every file this oracle counts as stranded is dirty, predates the most-recent-finalize boundary, and is not the in-flight work of any live session in this project -- and the briefing recommends a sweep only when that last clause is actually evidenced.
assertion.measures: git status --porcelain x file mtime vs HEAD's commit timestamp, minus paths found in live peers' registry dirtyFiles[] arrays (never written by any current session -- measured GitCellar 2026-08-12, ULDF 2026-08-16) and live peers' write journals (.claude/session-state/write-journal/<sessionId>.jsonl, tool-call records only); plus, since 1.3.0, each reported file's mtime against the EARLIEST live peer's registry spawnedAt (STRAND-02: a peer that had written the file would have set its mtime at or after its own start). The 'attribution' field grades which of those inputs actually supplied evidence, and 'provably_unowned' reports how much of the list the mtime proof covers.
known_gaps: Write journals are POSITIVE-ONLY: a script write or an external editor leaves no record, so a journal miss is not evidence of non-ownership. Handled: journals alone yield attribution 'journal-partial' and the sweep recommendation is withheld (never 'measured' and never 'predates-peers' -- the mtime proof is computed independently of journals precisely so this blindness cannot promote a grade).

attribution 'measured' is RESERVED AND UNPRODUCED framework-wide: nothing writes the registry dirtyFiles[] field (DISC-ORA-12), and as of DEC-372 nothing is planned to -- the file's owner refused the edit-path writer on cost, and no low-frequency seam can publish a COMPLETE set because a session knows its own tool calls, not its own writes (DEC-359: 158 of 244 spec-doc commits with no journal record from any session). The grade is kept because it is authoritative if a producer ever appears and because deployed consumers map it; the reachable top of the ladder is 'predates-peers' (STRAND-02). Read this as a declared ceiling on 'measured', not as pending work.

STRAND-02's proof is sound only against peers this oracle can SEE, and only while mtime tracks authorship. Three residuals, all narrower than the state it replaces: (a) a session that never registered, registered late, or whose workDir is spelled in a third form is invisible, so the earliest-start floor is computed over a subset -- the same registry-visibility bound 'no-peers' has always carried; (b) an mtime-preserving write (cp -p, tar/rsync with preserved times, touch -t) can leave an mtime older than the write, which is the same proxy caveat the boundary gate below already declares; (c) a peer whose FIRST registration happened after it had already written files would have a spawnedAt later than those writes. spawnedAt is preserved across RE-registration (hooks/session-start.sh) and a PODS roster row predates its worker's boot, so both ordinary paths err early -- the conservative direction.

A live peer registered with a workDir spelled in a third form this oracle's two-form (POSIX + Windows) case-insensitive comparison does not cover (e.g. a subst'd drive alias) would be invisible, driving the grade toward 'no-peers'/'unavailable'. Direction: 'no-peers' with an actually-live-but-unmatched peer is the residual wrong-sweep window; the two-form match covers every form the registry writers on this platform are known to produce.
mtime is a proxy for authorship time: a pre-boundary file touch-ed after the boundary escapes detection entirely (undercount, never a wrong sweep).

fallback: Run `git status --porcelain` to enumerate dirty files. Read `git log -1 --format=%aI HEAD` for last_finalize_at. For each dirty file, stat mtime and compare against last_finalize_at; if older AND no live peer claims it (per .claude/collaboration/active-sessions.json `dirtyFiles[]` registry field, defaulting to no-claim), it is a strand candidate. Cap sample at 10 entries; report full count separately. Above 2000 dirty files, skip detection.

detectionContract.summary: Stranded = (file in `git status --porcelain` dirty set) AND (mtime < HEAD's commit timestamp) AND (no live peer claims via dirtyFiles[] registry field).

ownership.source: .claude/collaboration/active-sessions.json sessions[] entries where status=='active' AND PID alive AND workDir matches this project root (POSIX or Windows form, case-insensitive -- DEFER-190: the bash twin's single-form match read 0 peers on Git Bash), plus each live peer's write journal .claude/session-state/write-journal/<sessionId>.jsonl
ownership.field: dirtyFiles[] (authoritative when present; never written by any current session -- DISC-ORA-12) + journal path records (positive-only) + each peer's spawnedAt as the STRAND-02 mtime-ordering floor (1.3.0). The 'attribution' output field grades which source supplied evidence; consumers gate sweep behavior on it (STRAND-01).

boundary.source: git log -1 --format=%aI HEAD (commit timestamp of HEAD; the most-recent-finalize boundary per spec acceptance §3)
boundary.rationale: The last committed timestamp is the project's effective finalize boundary; refined detection (parsing commit messages for /0-uldf-finalize markers) is deferred to Phase 1.7.1 if the simple boundary proves insufficient.

detectionContract.frozenSchema: The output schema is FROZEN at first commit. Programmatic consumers (/0-uldf-finalize --include-stranded partition logic; session-start hook briefing-line emission) read this shape. Changes require an explicit decision-channel entry plus LD approval — never silent.
